# SidewallMath

> Free tire size calculator. Type two sizes (265/70R17 vs 285/70R17) to see the % change, true speed, ride height, and sizes that fit your wheel. No signup.

URL: https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/
Last updated: 2026-10-19
Cost: free, no signup, runs in the browser.

## Key facts
- Overall diameter (in) = rim + 2 × sidewall; sidewall = section width (mm) × aspect ratio ÷ 100 ÷ 25.4. Circumference = π × diameter; revolutions per mile = 63,360 ÷ circumference.
- Example: 265/70R17 is 31.61 in tall, 10.43 in wide, with a 7.30 in sidewall and 638.1 revs per mile. 285/70R17 is 32.71 in tall (616.6 revs per mile).
- Swapping 265/70R17 for 285/70R17 makes the tire 1.10 in (3.49%) taller: 60 mph indicated is 62.09 mph actual, ride height rises about 0.55 in, and 10,000 indicated miles is 10,349 real miles.
- Verdict rule used: within 3% of the original diameter is a close match (a rule of thumb quoted by Discount Tire and 1010tires), over 3% up to 5% needs a clearance and speedometer check, over 5% is a big change. It is not a guarantee of fit.
- True speed = indicated speed × new diameter ÷ old diameter. Regear ratio to restore stock = axle ratio × new diameter ÷ old diameter. Engine RPM = mph × axle × transmission × 336.13 ÷ tire diameter (in).
- Backspacing (in) = (wheel width + 1) ÷ 2 + offset (mm) ÷ 25.4, assuming about 0.5 in of flange on each side. A 9 in wheel at 0 mm offset has 5.0 in backspacing.
- Sizes shown by the finder and converter are calculated combinations, not a list of tires that are sold. Real tire dimensions vary by brand and model, and loaded radius is a bit smaller.
- Planned domain sidewallmath.com is pending the owner's approval; the site is served at matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc.

## Tools (one page each)
- [Tire size calculator](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/tire-size-calculator/): Free tire size calculator. Compare two tire sizes (265/70R17 vs 285/70R17): % change, true speed, ride height, odometer error and a to-scale drawing. How it works: Overall height = wheel + 2 × (width in mm × aspect ratio ÷ 100) ÷ 25.4. The new height ÷ the old height gives the % change; true speed = indicated speed × new height ÷ old height. Within 3% is a close match, 3 to 5% needs a check, over 5% is a big change.
- [Tire size converter (metric to inches)](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/tire-size-converter/): Free tire size converter. Turn 265/70R17 into inches (31.6 x 10.4), or find the metric sizes for a 33 or 35 inch tire on your wheel size. How it works: Height in inches = wheel + 2 × (width mm × aspect ÷ 100) ÷ 25.4; width in inches = width mm ÷ 25.4. For inches to metric we try standard widths and aspect ratios on your wheel and list those within your tolerance, closest first.
- [Sizes that fit my wheel](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/tire-size-finder/): Free tire size finder. Enter your stock size to list calculated sizes within ±3% on the same, larger (plus) or smaller (winter) wheels, closest first. How it works: For each wheel size you choose, we try standard widths (155 to 355 mm) and aspect ratios (25 to 85) and keep those whose overall height is within your tolerance of stock, closest first.
- [Speedometer calculator](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/speedometer-calculator/): Free speedometer calculator. See your true speed and odometer error after a tire size change, or enter speedometer vs GPS to find the effective tire height. How it works: True speed = indicated speed × new tire height ÷ old tire height. Odometer miles scale the same way. In GPS mode, effective height = stock height × GPS speed ÷ speedometer speed.
- [Gear ratio calculator](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/gear-ratio-calculator/): Free gear ratio calculator. Enter stock and new tire sizes and your axle ratio to get the ratio that restores stock, the nearest common ratio and RPM at cruise. How it works: Acts like = axle × stock height ÷ new height. Ratio to restore stock = axle × new height ÷ stock height. RPM = mph × axle × top gear × 336.13 ÷ tire height in inches (336.13 = 63,360 ÷ (60 × π)).
- [Wheel offset calculator](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/wheel-offset-calculator/): Free wheel offset calculator. Enter old and new wheel width and offset to see backspacing, inner clearance and outer poke, with a to-scale cross-section. How it works: Backspacing = (width + 1) ÷ 2 + offset ÷ 25.4, assuming about ½ inch of flange on each side. Front spacing = width + 1 − backspacing. Inner clearance change = old − new backspacing; outer change = new − old front spacing.
- [Tire date code reader](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/tire-date-code/): Free tire date code reader. Enter the last four digits of the DOT code (like 2223) to see the week and year the tire was made and its age today. How it works: The last four digits of the DOT code are the week of manufacture (01 to 53) followed by the last two digits of the year. 2223 = week 22 of 2023. Age is counted from that week to today.

## Guides
- [How to read a tire size](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/how-to-read-a-tire-size/): How to read the numbers on a tire sidewall: P/LT/ST, width, aspect ratio, R/ZR, wheel size, load index, speed rating and the DOT date code, with an example.
- [Tire size chart](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/tire-size-chart/): Tire size chart for 15 to 22 inch wheels: overall height, width, sidewall and revs per mile for common sizes, every row linking to its own page.
- [Plus sizing explained](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/plus-sizing-explained/): What plus sizing is: a bigger wheel with a shorter sidewall that keeps the overall tire height within about 3%. Worked example 205/55R16 to 225/45R17 and 225/40R18.
- [Winter tire sizing](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/winter-tire-sizing/): How to size winter tires on a smaller wheel (minus sizing): calculated sizes that keep the overall height within about 2% of your stock tires, with worked examples.
- [Bigger tires and your speedometer](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/bigger-tires-speedometer/): Why a speedometer reads low with bigger tires, and by how much: true speed at 60 and 70 mph and the odometer error for 275/70R17 up to 35 inch tires.
- [Regear chart for bigger tires](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/regear-chart-for-bigger-tires/): Gear ratio needed to restore stock feel with 33, 35 or 37 inch tires, by current axle ratio (3.08 to 5.38) and stock tire height, calculated from the formula.
- [Tire speed rating chart](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/tire-speed-rating-chart/): Tire speed rating chart for the common sidewall letters S, T, H, V, W and Y with the maximum speed in mph and km/h, and what a speed rating does and does not mean.
- [Tire load index chart](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/tire-load-index-chart/): Tire load index chart from 70 to 126 with the maximum load per tire in kilograms and pounds, and how to read the number after the size, like 94 in 265/70R17 94T.
- [What size is a 31 inch tire?](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/what-size-is-a-31-inch-tire/): What metric size is a 31 inch tire? Calculated sizes within ½ inch of 31 in on 15 to 22 inch wheels (like 255/80R15), plus flotation sizes. Check availability.
- [What size is a 33 inch tire?](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/what-size-is-a-33-inch-tire/): What metric size is a 33 inch tire? Calculated sizes within ½ inch of 33 in on 15 to 22 inch wheels (like 305/75R15), plus flotation sizes. Check availability.
- [What size is a 35 inch tire?](https://matt5516.github.io/tire-size-calc/what-size-is-a-35-inch-tire/): What metric size is a 35 inch tire? Calculated sizes within ½ inch of 35 in on 15 to 22 inch wheels (like 315/80R15), plus flotation sizes. Check availability.

## FAQ
### How do I compare two tire sizes?
Convert each to overall diameter in inches: rim + 2 × (section width in mm × aspect ratio ÷ 100) ÷ 25.4. Then compare. 265/70R17 is 31.6 in tall and 285/70R17 is 32.7 in, a difference of 1.10 in or 3.5%.

### How much can I change tire size?
A common rule of thumb, used by Discount Tire's and 1010tires' calculators, is to stay within about 3% of the original overall diameter. It is a guideline, not a guarantee of fit: also check rim width, clearance, load index and speed rating.

### Will bigger tires change my speedometer?
Yes. The speedometer counts wheel turns, so a taller tire covers more ground per turn and the speedometer reads low. Going from 265/70R17 to 285/70R17, 60 mph on the speedometer is really 62.1 mph.

### What does 265/70R17 mean?
265 is the section width in millimetres, 70 is the sidewall height as a percentage of the width, R means radial construction and 17 is the wheel diameter in inches. That works out to a tire 31.6 in tall and 10.4 in wide.

### What size tire is 33 inches tall?
Many metric sizes land near 33 inches. On a 17 in wheel, 255/80R17 is 33.1 in tall, and on 20 in wheels 305/55R20 is 33.2 in. These are calculated: confirm a tire is actually made in that size.

### Do I need to regear for bigger tires?
Not always. Taller tires lower the effective gear ratio, so the engine turns slower at a given speed. The gear ratio calculator shows the ratio that restores stock and the nearest common ratio, plus engine RPM at your cruising speed.

### Does SidewallMath store my sizes?
No. Everything stays in your browser. Your sizes appear in the page link only so you can share a result.
